key_insight: Stopping freeze-thaw Bayesian optimization when no candidate’s expected improvement exceeds its incremental cost is simple and cost-aware, but can stop prematurely at low costs.
engineering_relevance: The rule provides a cost-aware reference for resumable hyperparameter tuning, trading model scores against training increments without requiring a fixed budget.
method: Maximize best observed score minus cost per training increment.
Under a fixed surrogate, advance the candidate with highest expected improvement; stop when none exceeds cost.
Use a lower bound on two-step lookahead value to certify premature stops; repeated corrections do not lower expected utility under the surrogate.
evidence_signal: Across three hyperparameter optimization benchmarks, a pre-registered test found EI stopping noninferior to the correction in most high-cost settings, while the correction gained at low costs on two benchmarks.
watch_item: Expected-utility guarantees depend on the surrogate; stronger information sharing improved EI stopping’s utility, highlighting sensitivity to surrogate design.
paper_title: Cost-Aware Stopping for Freeze-Thaw Bayesian Optimization: When Does One-Step Lookahead Suffice?
